articles.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, as expected; core inflation was higher than estimated
articles.description: The all-items consumer price index was expected to rise 0.4% in August, with core, excluding food and energy, showing a 0.2% gain, according to the Dow Jones consensus.
articles.content: Prices for a wide swath of goods and services continued to climb in August, according to a report Friday that could be the deciding factor on whether the Federal Reserve raises interest rates next wee... [849 symbols]
articles.summary: Consumer prices rose by 0.4% in August, as expected, but core inflation was higher than estimated. This could determine whether the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week. The consumer price index rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.3%, putting the 12-month increase at 3.4%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. However, stripping out volatile food and energy prices, core CPI posted a 0.2% monthly gain, 0.1 percentage point higher than forecast. The core annual rate came in at 2.4%. This is the final major inflation indicator the Fed will see before its policy meeting, which concludes with a vote on its key interest rate.
articles.shortSummary: In August, consumer prices rose 0.4% as expected, with core inflation higher than forecast, potentially influencing the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision next week.

The consumer price index, a broad measure of costs for goods and services across the U.S., fell by a seasonally adjusted 0.4% for the month, bringing the annual inflation rate down to 3.8%. However, core inflation, which excludes food and energy, remained steady at 2.6%.
articles.shortSummary: In June, US consumer prices rose by 0.4%, with annual growth of 3.5%, driven by energy costs, though overall they were lower than expected.

articles.content:

The closely watche... [6175 symbols]
articles.summary: US consumer price index is expected to rise by 0.1% in July, following a 0.4% decline in the previous month, according to a Bloomberg survey. This is seen as a welcome sign of easing inflationary pressures following the recent war-driven rise. This comes after three Federal Reserve officials voted to raise interest rates despite a weak July jobs report. The report is likely to show a cooling of energy-related price pressures, which had intensified following the start of the US war with Iran. Retail gasoline prices dropped to a four-month low before climbing back above $4 a gallon late in the month, and airfares may also decrease as jet-fuel costs settle back. China's July inflation data will also be released, with consumer inflation expected to slow to 0.8%, while factory-gate price growth may ease to 3.8%. Other countries releasing revised data for second-quarter GDP include Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore. The UK is expectedly to publish growth numbers on Friday, showing resilience to the West Asia crisis.
articles.shortSummary: US CPI is expected to rise 0.1 per cent in July, easing inflationary pressures after a six-year low, while key economic data sets the stage for future interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Consumer prices continued to climb in August, as inflation concerns persist

articles.content:

The rhetoric was wrong but familiar. In fac... [2370 symbols]
articles.summary: Consumer prices continued to climb in August, raising concerns about inflation. The consumer price index rose by 0.4% seasonally adjusted, bringing the 12-month increase to 3.4%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. However, excluding food and energy, prices rose by only 0.3% last month, which was worse than expected. This is the fifth consecutive inflation rate has been higher than wages, exacerbating affordability issues for consumers. The rise in oil prices predate the recent sharp rise in crude prices, which led to higher energy costs and higher petroleum prices. The data suggests that September may be even worse.

Consumer prices remained elevated in August as the Iran war's energy shock fueled a fresh burst of inflation .

Why it matters: The renewed price pressures are squeezing household budgets, with signs ... [1690 symbols]
articles.summary: Consumer prices remained high in August, rising by 0.4% from the previous month due to the Iran war's energy shock. The Labor Department reported that consumer prices rose by 3.4%, a year earlier, and excluding volatile food and energy costs, the core gauge climbed 0.3% during the month and 2.4%. This is seen as a significant increase for the Federal Reserve, which is expected to consider a rate hike if inflation continues to rise. This could complicate efforts by the Trump administration to convince voters that affordability is improving. Oil prices are currently hovering around $100 a barrel, up from about $80 in mid-August, and diesel prices hit a record $6 per gallon.
articles.shortSummary: Inflation rose in August as the Iran war's energy shock increased energy costs, squeezing household budgets, ahead of the Fed's interest rate decision next week.

The CPI rose by 0.,1% in July, and in the 12 months through August, consumer inflation advanced by 3.4%. The rise in the Producer Price Index also boosted rate increase prospects.
articles.shortSummary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, driven by a rebound in petrol prices, boosting potential interest rate hikes next week.

articles.shortSummary: Consumer prices slowed in June due to lower energy and gasoline prices, but inflation risks re-igniting amid renewed tensions with Iran and potentially raising interest rates.

articles.title: The Fed's big inflation test
articles.description: A run of economic data has bolstered the case for a rate hike, including a rise in core consumer prices.
articles.content:
The Fed looks boxed into raising interest rates next week after Friday morning's hot inflation report . Less certain is what comes after that.

Why it matters: August inflation was shaping up to be a ... [1571 symbols]
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise interest rates next week after a hot inflation report revealed a significant increase in August. The core Consumer Price Index, excluding volatile food and energy costs, showed more momentum than the headline figures indicated. This follows Fed chairman Kevin Warsh's warning that rising price pressures could warrant tighter policy. Investors now see an 85% chance of a rate increase at the Fed's meeting next Wednesday, up from 72% before the inflation data. This puts Warsh on a tightrope as bond markets currently price in multiple interest rate increases.
articles.shortSummary: The Fed faces a crucial inflation test with a potential interest rate hike next week, as underlying inflation shows more momentum and potential future rate hikes.

articles.content:
In the battle of the two major concerns in the U.S. economy, this week it is inflation’s turn.

Last week provided a surprise with a loss of in July rather than the increase of around 83,000 that had ... [2256 symbols]
articles.summary: Inflation could increase in July, with the consumer price index for July expected to drop to a lower annual rate of 3.4%, from 3.5% in June and 4.2% in May. This could help the Federal Reserve avoid raising interest rates in September, but could raise concerns about job growth and the economy's underlying growth. Economists attribute this decrease to less volatility in gasoline prices. The August jobs data and CPI report will come out before the Fed meets, so the July reports are not the final word. However, there are also expected to be readings on Friday of July's retail sales and the University of Michigan's first estimate for August from both.
articles.shortSummary: Inflation could impact job growth and economic growth more significantly as key July CPI and producer price reports are expected to show signs of cooling down, potentially delaying interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Inflation relief's staying power is in question
articles.description: July brought plenty of heat, but very little of it showed up in consumer prices.
articles.content:
Inflation was benign in July, a second month of relief for American consumers and economic policymakers contending with stubborn price pressures.

Why it matters: The tame reading might give the Feder... [3177 symbols]
articles.summary: Inflation was benign in July, giving the Federal Reserve some breathing room to hold off raising interest rates. However, the Iran war and fluctuating energy prices have raised questions about the staying power of this relief. The Consumer Price Index rose only 0.1% in July after falling 0.4% in June, while the year-over-year inflation rate dropped to 3.4%, from 3.5%. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, advanced 0.2% and was up 2.5% from a year earlier, down from 2.6%. However, there is little evidence of these price pressures expanding into the core inflation gauge the Fed watches most closely. Other potential inflationary factors like tariffs and the AI buildout remain risks. Financial markets now see the chance of an interest rate increase as less likely.
articles.shortSummary: Inflation eased in July, but sustainability concerns remain amid rising oil prices and potential inflationary factors, with the Federal Reserve potentially delaying interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Austrian inflation rises on higher fuel costs
articles.description: Austria's consumer price inflation accelerated as initially estimated in August amid higher fuel and heating oil prices, the latest data from Statistics Austria, the country's official statistics agency, showed on Thursday. The consumer price index climbed 3.
articles.content: Austria's consumer price inflation accelerated as initially estimated in August amid higher fuel and heating oil prices, the latest data from Statistics Austria, the country's official statistics agen... [1039 symbols]

keywords.name: higher fuel and heating oil prices

articles.summary: Austria's consumer price inflation accelerated in August due to higher fuel and heating oil prices, according to Statistics Austria. The consumer price index climbed 3.2% year-over-year in August, faster than the 2.8% increase in July. Inflation in transport rose to 7.8%, from 6.4%, due to a 26.3% surge in fuel costs. Annual price growth in housing and utilities also accelerated to 3.3%. Costs related to restaurants and accommodation services were 4.7% higher. The reduction in value-added tax on basic foodstuffs from 10% to 4.9% helped moderate price pressures. The European Union measure of inflation, the harmonized index of consumer prices, rose 2.9%.
articles.shortSummary: Austria's consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.2% in August due to higher fuel and heating oil costs, with transport costs rising sharply and housing costs falling.

articles.title: US consumer prices drop in June as energy costs tumble
articles.description: Inflation eased due to cheaper energy, but experts warn price increases may return after renewed US-Iran tensions.
articles.content:

Consumer prices in the United States tumbled in June as energy prices fell, led by c... [3349 symbols]
articles.summary: Consumer prices in the US fell in June, largely due to cheaper energy prices, but experts warn that further increases may return due to renewed US-Iran tensions. Energy prices fell by 5.7 percent, marking the biggest monthly decline since April 2020. Oil prices saw the biggest drop, with petrol prices dropping 9.5 percent. The average price for a gallon of petrol (3.85) is $3.05, down from $4.07 at this time last month. Other sectors saw declines in consumer prices including apparel, used car or truck, and electricity. The annual CPI rose by 3.5% after a 4.2 percent increase in May, the largest annual increase in over three years.
articles.shortSummary: US consumer prices fell in June due to cheaper energy, but experts warn price increases may return amid renewed US-Iran tensions.

articles.title: Consumer prices fall for first time since early days of COVID pandemic, but war against high inflation isn't won
articles.content:
Plunge in gas prices during recent Iran cease-fire brought some relief. Renewed conflict poses fresh threat.

Gasoline prices might start rising again due to renewed hostilities between the U.S. and I... [4240 symbols]
articles.summary: Consumer prices fell for the first time in six years in June, largely due to plunging gas prices, but the battle against high inflation is still not over. The consumer-price index dropped by 0.4% last month, marking the first drop since May 2020. This decline was twice as large as Wall Street had predicted. However, renewed conflict between the U.S. and Iran could lead to gasoline prices rising again due to renewed hostilities. The yearly inflation rate also slowed to 3.5% from a three-year high of 4.2%. Despite this, the June CPI showed progress, with the core rate that strips out food and energy being flat, coming in below the Wall Street forecast of a 0.2% increase. New Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is testifying before Congress to outline his inflation-fighting strategy.
articles.shortSummary: Plunge in gas prices reduced US consumer prices in June, but high inflation remains a threat to economic stability amid renewed conflict with Iran, with potential rate hikes expected.
